title: Three equal export files
prompt: A partner loads the invoice lines with three workers, one file each. Finish `write_export` so the Delta table it writes has exactly three data files of about the same size. `layout` reports the files from the log.
rules: The table has three data files, and every line is in one of them. With no lines there are no files.
File sizes differ by at most one line.
hints: Run the starter and check `files`: how many partitions does `invoice_lines` have when it's read?
A write makes one file per partition that has rows. Which call can make more partitions than there are?
`coalesce` can only merge partitions. `repartition(n)` shuffles the rows evenly into `n`.
explanation: `invoice_lines` is read from one small file, so it has one partition and the write makes one file. `repartition(3)` shuffles the rows round-robin into three partitions whose sizes differ by at most one, so the write makes three files: for ten lines, 4, 3 and 3. `coalesce(3)` can't help: it only merges partitions, and there's just one to start with. A cap with `maxRecordsPerFile` set to a third of the lines rounded up gives three files too, but the last one is short: 4, 4 and 2.
